extraction.name: CADS: A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography
extraction.description: An open-source framework and large-scale CT dataset for whole-body anatomical segmentation with 22,022 CT volumes and 167 anatomical structures, plus trained models and a 3D Slicer plugin.
extraction.creator: Murong Xu, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Femando Navarro, Maksym Fritsak, Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Suprosanna Shit, Bastian Wittmann, Sezgin Er, Sebastian M. extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was aggregated from more than 40 sources, including public archives (e.g., TCIA), medical imaging challenges (via Grand Challenge and MICCAI), focused research studies, and newly acquired hospital CT scans. The authors also added manual annotations from in-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist, and used pseudo-labeling, self-training, shape-guided quality control, and ensemble selection to generate whole-body annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 79% of the initial collection did not include any manual annotations; only 4,695 of 22,022 volumes (about 21%) contained partial annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CT volumes from public archives (including TCIA), challenge datasets (e.g., TotalSegmentator, VISCERAL, Han-Seg, SAROS, KiTS, LiTS, BTCV, CHAOS, VerSe, etc.), and newly acquired anonymized head CT scans and triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans from hospital collaborators.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Missing annotations were filled using pseudo-labeling and self-training. Specialized models generated pseudo-labels for unlabeled scans, low-quality pseudo-labels were filtered using shape-space outlier detection, and final labels were assembled by selecting the best-performing model flavor per structure; original ground-truth annotations replaced pseudo-labels when available.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All images were standardized by reorienting to RAS, resampling to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, simplifying affine transforms by removing rotation and translation, and applying Gaussian blurring to facial regions of newly acquired head CTs for privacy.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were standardized to consistent orientation and resolution; scans with inadequate head coverage were excluded for head-region labeling; scans with low-quality pseudo-labels were filtered out; intermediate slices without annotations were excluded for SAROS; transitional vertebrae cases were excluded for VerSe evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created from existing manual labels, additional manual annotations by three medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist, registration-derived brain labels, interpolation of sparse slice annotations, pseudo-label generation, shape-based quality control, and final label assembly with GT priority. Rib labels were further refined to correct fragmentation and retrieve costovertebral joints.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Three model flavors (GT, pseudo, shape) were compared using Dice and HD95; statistical ranking used Shapiro-Wilk, Levene’s test, ANOVA/Welch’s ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis, and post-hoc tests (Tukey’s HSD or Dunn’s test) to choose the final label source per structure. Expert review was also used to curate unreliable ground-truth annotations in TotalSegmentator.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Varies by source; many scans had no annotations, some had partial annotations for one or two structures, and the final dataset provides voxel-level annotations for 167 structures.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three in-house medical research assistants and one radiation oncologist contributed manual annotations; an experienced radiation oncologist (5.5 years in practice) performed expert review.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net, neural implicit functions, ANTS, vesselFM, Seg-metrics, surface-distance, TPTBox
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, models, and plugin are publicly released via Hugging Face and GitHub; no explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Age (patients aged ≥18 years for newly acquired head CTs), geography/country of acquisition, and facial features were handled with anonymization; the dataset also includes pathological conditions and disease sites.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to improve clinical radiation therapy planning, diagnostic radiology, and broader anatomical analysis by providing robust AI tools and accessible software for clinicians and researchers.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset spans 16 countries and over 100 centers, but the paper notes potential biases from protocol heterogeneity, inter-annotator inconsistency, class imbalance, and the fact that some structures are underrepresented or absent in current datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include exclusion of some atypical cases during evaluation, incomplete coverage beyond head-to-knee, remaining refinement needs for several structures (e.g., brain mask, optic chiasm, heart, rectum, trachea, vena cava), and anonymized facial features that limit detailed facial analysis.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, testing, fine-tuning, and clinical deployment support for whole-body CT segmentation; also intended for radiation therapy planning, diagnostic radiology, and research applications.
